claims.text: Conventionally PVD-deposited elemental Cr coatings on Zircaloy typically have columnar or polycrystalline microstructures.
Elemental Cr coatings possess inherent oxidation resistance.
Elemental Cr coatings on Zircaloy are susceptible to interfacial Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
A post-deposition nitrogen plasma treatment can induce nitridation at or near the Cr/Zircaloy interface.
The nitrogen plasma treatment can form a continuous CrN interlayer a few tens of nanometers thick.
The resulting CrN interlayer will be dense, uniform, and nanocrystalline.
A dense nanocrystalline CrN interlayer will act as a Cr–Zr diffusion barrier.
The nitrided coating will maintain a protective passivated surface.
CrN has very low atomic diffusivity.
Interfacial CrN will hinder Cr–Zr interdiffusion and stabilize the coating microstructure.
CrN will maintain robust oxidation resistance during both low-temperature reactor operation and high-temperature steam exposure.
Relative to unmodified Cr, the nitrided Cr coating will exhibit significantly less interfacial Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to unmodified Cr, the nitrided coating will have enhanced thermal stability.
Relative to unmodified Cr, the nitrided coating will have improved oxidation performance.
Reduced interdiffusion, enhanced thermal stability, and improved oxidation performance will prolong coating life under both reactor and accident conditions.
Unmodified elemental Cr coatings can perform adequately in individual service regimes but fail under combined service conditions.
The degradation of the unmodified Cr coating is caused by interfacial interdiffusion.
The proposed intervention is applicable at approximately 320 °C in pressurized water and up to approximately 1200 °C in steam for exposures lasting tens of hours.
